cues.zh: 大家好，我是 Emre Berger，今天我要讲的是性能问题。
cues.en: Hi everybody, so I'm Emre Berger, I'm going to be talking today about performance matters.

cues.en: This is joint work with my former PhD student Charlie Kertsinger.

cues.en: So I'm going to tell you a story that happened a short time ago in a valley far far away.

cues.en: So, the story is about a character who we're going to call Luke.

cues.en: Luke is our hero, and of course he's a hero in Silicon Valley because Luke has an idea for an app.

cues.en: All right, so here is Luke's genius idea for an app.

cues.zh: 基本上就是，你用智能手机拍下东西的照片，然后它会去找匹配的结果并返回给你。
cues.en: Basically you use your smartphone and you take pictures of things, and then it goes and finds matches like and returns them to you.

cues.zh: 他还给它起了个很棒的名字，叫 Ogggle。
cues.en: And he's got a great name for it as well, he's going to call it Ogggle.

cues.en: And he's pretty sure Ogggle is going to totally disrupt image search.

cues.en: Nobody has told him about Google image search yet, but anyway.

cues.zh: 于是他着手把它做出来，做出了原型 Ogggle。
cues.en: So he sets about building it, so he makes the prototype Ogggle.

cues.zh: 好，Ogggle 原型是这样工作的：拍一张照片，照片会被发送到 Ogggle 数据中心。
cues.en: Right, so the prototype Ogggle works like this, take a picture, it gets sent off to the Ogggle data center.

cues.zh: 如果这张图是新的，就会被加入数据库，同时它还会去找相似图片，并把它们发回给用户。
cues.en: If it is new, it gets added to the database, and then at the same time it goes and finds similar pictures and sends them back to the user.

cues.zh: 好，所以这个过程相当简单直接。
cues.en: All right, so this is pretty straightforward.

cues.zh: 你可以把这个流程抽象一下，可以这样想：收到一个请求，请求进来后，基本上会启动两个线程，其中一个去取图片，假设把它压缩一下，然后保存到一张 3.5 英寸软盘上。
cues.en: You can kind of abstract out this flow, if you think of it as follows, you get a request, the request comes in, it essentially spawns two threads, one of them goes and takes the image and let's say compresses it, and then saves it to a three and a half inch floppy.

cues.zh: 就像大家都会做的那样，然后同时它会做一些索引来查找匹配。
cues.en: As one does, and then at the same time it does some indexing to look up matches.

cues.zh: 对，所以它先做一些特征提取，然后进行搜索，再通过纸飞机把结果发回给用户。
cues.en: Right, so it does a search, after doing some feature extraction, and then sends it back to the user via paper airplane.

cues.zh: 这是人类已知最有效的方法。
cues.en: Which is the most effective method known to man.

cues.zh: 然后最终这两个线程会汇合。
cues.en: And then eventually these two threads join up.

cues.zh: 好了，这显然是个简化版，我省略了一些东西，比如锁。
cues.en: All right, so this is obviously a simplification, I've alluded certain things, like for example locks.

cues.zh: 所以当有锁的时候，对吧，比如有个数据库，你不能同时修改数据库，等等等等。
cues.en: So when you have locks, right, there's some database for example, you can't be modifying the database simultaneously, blah blah blah.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，这基本上就是 Ogggle 工作方式的高层概览。
cues.en: But anyway, this is essentially at a high level how Ogggle is going to work.

cues.en: But then, as the number of users kind of like mount, it turns out Ogggle starts getting slow.

cues.en: And on the right you have clock speed, which roughly corresponds to computing performance.

cues.zh: 所以基本上，很多很多年里，我们都处在这样一种情况：晶体管数量大约每 18 个月翻一番。
cues.en: And so, basically for years and years and years, we had this situation where the number of transistors were increasing roughly at doubling every 18 months.

cues.zh: 这就是著名的摩尔定律。
cues.en: This is famously Moore's Law.

cues.zh: 这通常带来的效果是，让时钟频率得以提升。
cues.en: And this generally had the effect of allowing clock speed to increase.

cues.zh: 所以特征尺寸变小了，这意味着你的程序实际会跑得更快。
cues.en: And so you had smaller features, this meant that your programs would actually run faster.

cues.zh: 而事实上，你几乎只要等着就行。
cues.en: And in fact, you could just literally wait.

cues.zh: 对，如果你买新硬件，实际上升级周期——你知道，大概每年左右——比如你买了台新电脑，一切都会快得多。
cues.en: Right, if you buy new hardware, in fact, the upgrade cycle, every you know, every year or so, like if you bought a new computer, everything would run much faster.

cues.zh: 那很糟。
cues.en: It was bad.

cues.zh: 对，从 33 兆赫兹到 66 兆赫兹，当时很牛，今天却挺糟糕的，对吧？
cues.en: Right, 33 megahertz to 66 was awesome back then, and kind of terrible today, okay?

cues.zh: 但它确实改变了“做性能优化的人”这件事的格局。
cues.en: But it did change the landscape of what it meant to be somebody who works on performance improvement.

cues.zh: 因为这就是你会做的事，对吧？
cues.en: Because this is what you would do, right?

cues.zh: 所以某种程度上，如果某个东西的性能 18 个月就会翻倍，费劲去榨出性能真没什么意义。
cues.en: So there really in a way was no sense trying to squeeze out any performance out of something, when it was going to double in 18 months.

cues.zh: 对，你指望在 18 个月里榨出双倍性能，机会很渺茫，那还不如去海滩上喝莫吉托。
cues.en: Right, the chance that you in 18 months were going to squeeze out double the performance, pretty slender, so you might as well just sip mojitos on the beach.

cues.zh: 好吧？
cues.en: All right?

cues.zh: 我可以告诉你，嗯，也许莫吉托和海滩那部分除外，这……
cues.en: I can tell you that this was well maybe the mojitos and beach part notwithstanding.

cues.zh: 这其实算是高性能计算领域推荐的一种策略。
cues.en: This was actually kind of a strategy that was recommended for high-performance computing.

cues.zh: 人们真的会说，我们明年或者后年直接升级电脑就行了。
cues.en: People would literally say, we're just going to upgrade the computers next year or in two years.

cues.zh: 所以把精力放在别的事情上。
cues.en: So focus on something else.

cues.zh: 别关注性能。
cues.en: Don't focus on performance.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.en: Now, unfortunately, that's not the current state of affairs, right, so today as all of you know, when you upgrade a computer, it does not get faster anymore.

cues.zh: 也许它变轻了，也许电池续航提升了。
cues.en: Maybe it gets lighter, maybe it has improved battery life.

cues.zh: 嗯，也许并没有。
cues.en: Um, maybe not.

cues.zh: 但基本上，最终摩尔定律渐渐失去了动力。
cues.en: But, but basically what happened is eventually Moore's law kind of ran out of steam.

cues.zh: 原因其实并不是摩尔定律真的失效了。
cues.en: The reason that it did is not actually, it's not actually true that Moore's Law ran out of steam.

cues.zh: 严格来说，这是一个叫登纳德缩放的问题。
cues.en: This is technically a problem called Denard Scaling.

cues.zh: 登纳德缩放失效了，所以现在的情况是，如果提高时钟频率，我们已经无法有效散掉芯片上的热量，让它们跑得更快。
cues.en: Um, and so Denard scaling ran out, and so right now we're in a situation where basically if we clock things up, we no longer can dissipate the heat on chips effectively enough to make them run faster.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以晶体管数量其实还在增加，这就是为什么我们有多核。
cues.en: Um, so transistor counts actually are still increasing, which is why we have multiple cores.

cues.zh: 呃，我们有一大堆晶体管，那拿它们干什么呢？
cues.en: Uh, so we have a bunch of transistors, what are we going to do with them?

cues.zh: 那就批量多造一些同样的东西吧。
cues.en: Let's just stamp out more of the same thing.

cues.zh: 对，这很好，但也没那么棒，因为如果你的程序不是并行的，它不会跑得更快。
cues.en: Right, so that's great, but it's also not super awesome because if you have a program that is not parallel, it's not going to run any faster.

cues.zh: 所以，嗯，现在什么都是多核的，你的手机也是多核。
cues.en: So, um, everything now has multi-core, your phone has multi-core.

cues.zh: 但事实证明，这仍然是个问题。
cues.en: But it turns out, it's still a problem.
